text:
Allergies:
Spironolactone / Levaquin

Chief Complaint:
shortness of breath

History of Present Illness:
___ year old ___ gentleman with HBV cirrhosis and 
hepatocellular carcinoma with prior ascites and encephalopathy 
now presenting with increasing shortness of breath and DOE and 
increasing ___ edema x weeks. Of note his daughters believe he 
has gained 20 lbs since ___.

The patient was in his usual state of health until ___ when 
he was admitted for dyspnea and treated for a COPD flare. He 
returned home but since that time his daughters believe he has 
had expanding abdominal girth as well as a ___. He also developed 
a lower extremity and buttock rash.

He was admitted to ___ ~2 weeks prior to the current admission 
for multiple concerns including family concern over ascites and 
new petechial rash. Now diagnosed with leukocytoclastic 
vasculitis.

Doing ok at home since then but with gradually increasing SOB 
and DOE as well as worsening ___ edema to the point where he can 
barely walk and cannot bend his knees due to the edema.

On the morning of admission his SOB was even worse. Daughters 
also noting decreased UOP across past 24 hours.

He went for f/u derm and CT scan this morning and then decided 
to see PCP's office where he was evaluated by urgent care. They 
sent him to the ED with concern for decompensated liver failure 
and possible SBP.

In ED patient was afebrile, hr 67. bp 146/75 and saturating 100% 
on 2L. Labs and abdominal US were performed. CT scan from this 
morning showing new pleural effusions. U/S showing patent portal 
vein. Scrotal edema noted on exam.

Daughters also noting some chills in last 24 hours but no 
fevers. Believe he is having some chest tightness with exertion 
(stairs). Per daughters at present needs to stop 3 times when 
walking up the stairs at home.

No fever, night sweats, no nausea or vomiting, no change in 
bowel habits (baseline loose stools ___ lactulose).

Review of systems:
(+) Per HPI
(-) Denies fever, night sweats, recent weight loss, headache, 
sinus tenderness, rhinorrhea or congestion. Denied cough, 
nausea, vomiting, diarrhea (aside from regular lactulose induced 
BMs), constipation or abdominal pain (aside from baseline 
intermittent RUQ pain). No recent change in bowel or bladder 
habits. No dysuria. Denied arthralgias or myalgias.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ h/o HBV cirrhosis, HCC, CHF, CKD and COPD p/w increasing 
SOB/DOE x weeks, family report of increased ascites and 20lb 
weight gain over past month, and decreased UOP x 1 day. No 
fevers, possible chills, no abdominal pain, no change in bowel 
habits. New pleural effusions on Chest CT. Abdominal US with 
moderate ascites and patent portal veins.

# Pleural Effusions: most likely ___ CHF but cannot r/o 
malignant effusions given history of lung nodule. If CHF mixed 
systolic (LVEF 45%) and diastolic, exacerbated by stopping 
diuretics due to rising creatinine now with significant pleural 
effusions and reported 20 lbs weight gain. Put out 1.5L after 
10mg IV lasix. Treated with therapeutic thoracentesis.

# IDDM/Hypoglycemia: per glucometer and daughters recently 
widely ranging sugars in 100s to 400s. Takes lantus at night 
(now 26 units) and RISS, checks 4/day. Rec'd 20 units of 
glargine (less than his home dose) on the night of admission. On 
second day or hospitalization had ___ 166, got 4 units RISS, ate 
breakfast, went to thoracentesis. Shortly after he became 
hypoglycemic to 40 and unarousable. Gave D50 and patient woke 
right up. Lantus dose reduced.

# Decompensated Liver Failure: Family concerned about abdominal 
ascites although limited evidence of ascites on exam with only 
minor distention (compared to previous admission) and no 
appreciable fluid wave. U/S still showing only mild ascites 
without any drainable fluid, abdominal exam mildly tense but 
non-tender. Unlikely SBP absent fever, abdominal pain or 
tenderness or mental status changes. Continued on lactulose and 
spironalactone.

# Scrotal Edema and Penile Bulge: most likely simply scrotal 
edema plus penile edema in the setting of significant fluid 
overload. Lack of pain makes paraphimosis less likely. No 
history of injury to suggest vascular compromise. Per urology 
only a medical emergency if evidence of restricting blood flow. 
Urology consulted and felt swelling was ___ edema and did not 
require surgical intervention. 

# Transaminitis: ___ Hep B and HCC. Minorly elevated but overall 
consistent with recent values; total bili, which was elevated on 
recent admission to 3.2, is now resolved. No signs of acutely 
deteriorating synthetic function, Alb 2.6 INR 1.1. No mental 
status changes. Abd US showing only small perihepatic fluid. 
Continued on lamivudine and lactulose.

# Cirrhosis ___ HBV: admitted with family concern for increasing 
abdominal girth, no fluid wave on exam, U/S showing some 
perihepatic fluid but no drainable ascites, last para ___, no 
evidence of SBP. Continued on home regimen of lactulose, 
nadolol, rifaximin and lamivudine. Restarted spironalactone.

# CAD: no evidence of active CAD, previous pMIBI ___ with 
reversible defect, multiple risk factors including HTN DMII HLD. 
Continued on ASA, statin, nadolol. ACEi decision deferred to 
outpatient in the setting of recent renal insufficiency.

# CKI: creatinine 1.4 at or below baseline (~1.5). Reduced UOP 
x1 day in setting of significant penile swelling possibly 
leading to retention resolved with resolution of edema.

# ___ petechial rash. Similar to on previous admission, in 
dependent areas, appears c/w petechiae/purpura c/f vasculitis. 
Evaluated by derm on prior admission and punch biopsies taken. 
Patient about to f/u with derm at time of admission. Sutures 
removed on day of admission by derm nurse. Preliminary 
differential includes LCV (with possibly causes being LVQ which 
he is no longer taking vs hepatitis), thrombocytopenic purpura 
(unlikely given platelets ~50-60) vs other 
vasculitis/vasculopathy.

# Normocytic Anemia. Chronically falling HCT since ___, 
from HCT ~45 to HCT ~29 now. HD stable. Some concern for 
hemachromatosis. Consideration for starting erythropoetin but 
felt most appropriately deferred to outpatient setting.

# ___ fungal rash on feet: Distinct from petechial rash mentioned 
above. Continued anti-fungal ointment.

# COPD: mild, continued on home regimen of nebulizers.

# ITEMS FOR OUTPATIENT FOLLOW UP:
-potassium and creatinine on lasix
-concern for hemachromatosis; consider ordering hemachromatosis 
mutation test
-consider starting lisinopril
-follow hct and adjust erythropoietin as needed

Discharge Diagnosis:
PRIMARY:
1. CHF
2. COPD
3. Cirrhosis

SECONDARY:
1. CKI
